QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_12

question.text: Suryoday Impact Fund has fully exited all portfolio investments and wound up. At wind-up:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.4.4 behaviour point 3: 'By the time the fund has fully exited all its investments, the DPI becomes complete and the RVPI is reduced to zero. At this stage DPI = TVPI.' Once every position is realised, there is no residual NAV, so RVPI collapses to zero and TVPI equals DPI. The Trap: The first distractor describes mid-life behaviour (residual value still present), not wind-up. The option claiming DPI > TVPI and RVPI < 0 is mathematically impossible because RVPI cannot be negative (it is a ratio of non-negative fair value). The option RVPI = TVPI and DPI = 0 reverses the wind-up relationship — at wind-up DPI equals TVPI, not RVPI. Note: Reworded the trap paragraph so it correctly identifies the impossible distractor (negative RVPI) rather than calling the keyed correct option impossible, and removed the cross-exam/pro-tip lines that were not source-grounded.
